title: formula: a capability predicate in the standard library — a page predicate can ask whether the viewer holds a system capability, from the same data the action gate reads (cloud#3036 ruling A)
body:
Filed by the director seat (summon #43 continuation 5, `session_01QJC7i981TSs9L1CGJK59Ax`) from objectstack-ai/cloud#3036, ruled A by the maintainer on 2026-10-19 (batch #366 item 4): the action's declaration is the one source of truth, so a page predicate must be able to ask the same question the action gate asks — does the viewer hold this capability. Platform first (the maintainer's 口径 「平台相关的功能，应该尽量先改平台。」). ⛔ Not a claim. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — one new standard-library function.

## What is measured (cloud#3036 os-dev-report 6255664506; objectui `9e7e1a55bead`, objectstack `44a5011fe623`)
- `packages/formula/src/stdlib.ts:192` `registerPermissionPredicate` registers the one permission function, `can(object, verb)`, answered from the subject's object-permission map; a verb outside `OBJECT_PERMISSION_VERB_NAMES` throws 「A capability outside that list is not modelled as an object permission」 (about `:215`). No function answers a `systemPermissions` name.
- objectui binds a page predicate's `current_user` from `buildExpressionUser` (`packages/app-shell/src/providers/expressionUser.ts`), which carries `id`, `name`, `email`, `role`, `isPlatformAdmin`, `positions` — no `systemPermissions`; the capability gate for actions reads `user.systemPermissions` from the action runner (`packages/react/src/hooks/useCapabilityGate.ts:40`–`:49`). So actions are gated on capabilities and no page node can be.
- The proxy cloud pages use today (`can('sys_environment','edit')`) diverges from the capability for a platform administrator who is a plain member of an organisation (measured).

## What changes
- `packages/formula` standard library: one predicate (name chosen by the lane; for example `hasCapability(name)` on the subject, beside `can`), answered from the subject's held system capabilities (the `systemPermissions` list `GET /api/v1/auth/me/permissions` returns). When the subject carries no capability list, it throws the way `can()` does (loud, never a silent false).
- The subject contract: the evaluator's subject gains the capability list beside the object-permission map (`packages/core/src/evaluator/subjectPermissions.ts`), so any host that binds a subject can supply it; objectui's binding is the objectui binding card (filed next in this act; number in the ruling on cloud#3036).
- Docs: the predicate's describe and the spec's `visible` / `visibleWhen` docs name it as the way to gate a page node on a capability (ADR-0066 D4 stays: `visible` hides, `requiredPermissions` refuses).
- Tests: held / not held / list absent (throws); a name with no declaring action is still just a string (no registry lookup).

## Acceptance
- `pnpm check` green; generated baselines by tooling; changeset `minor` on `@objectstack/formula` (and `@objectstack/core` if the subject type changes).
- Review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (a new public function, `Clause-②: yes`).

## Dispatch notes
- Not governed. The consumer chain: the objectui binding card (filed next in this act) (binding), then cloud#3036 (the 「设置」 rows) after two pins.
